After persistence, bridgit:answered lets the card show its confirmation; the trusted Back to questions control reloads the question for resubmission. Bridgit.act({method, path, query?, body?}) runs one of your own endpoints on the phone right away, as you, with your grants and the owner's switches, e.g. await Bridgit.act({path:'/v1/flashlight', body:{on:true, auto_off_seconds:1}}) resolves to {ok, status, body}. A request is at most 16 KB (bigger: error request_too_big, so send a capture_id or gallery_id, never photo bytes) and a JSON reply over 64 KB comes back ok: false, error reply_too_big with the fix (ask for less). You get an action.executed event for each call, so it works while you're offline. A single card can't be swiped: show progress as text ("Step 2 of 5"), not swipe or segment bars. expires_in_s.description: Stop after this long, up to 86400 (default 7200). With a tally: up to 7776000 (90 days, default 30 days)

sound.description: With data ["sound"]: {sensitivity: quiet | normal (default) | loud (how much louder than the room's quiet level a sound must be), reuse_s: 0-1800 (default 300; a loud sound this soon after the last paid check that sounds like it, compared on the phone by its frequency fingerprint, reuses that answer for free (answered_locally, similarity in last_check); a different-sounding one is checked; 0 = ask every time)}. No interval_s: the phone's loudness check wakes the watch, at most once every 30 s. Model must be clef. Paid checks default to 6 an hour; set max_paid_per_hour to change it. Needs the sounds permission and switch and the microphone permission. The watch shows listening true/false and not_listening_reason

questions.description: Instead of question: 1-10 typed questions, {id: {type: choice|noul, instructions, criteria?}}, as https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives

rules.description: With tally: up to 5 rules the phone checks after every reading. {id, when, do?, cooldown_s?}. when: {none_for_s, of, while_seen?: true} (no episode of that label for so long; while_seen counts only watched time), {fewer_than, of, by: "10:00"} (fewer episodes today by that local time; once a day), or {at_least, of, within_s}. A rule that fires sends you a watch.rule event {watch_id, rule, message, today, action} and runs do, exactly one of: {"flow":"<workflow id>", "with"?: {…}} starts one of your called or button workflows (its steps read the rule as {"$trigger":"message"}, "of", "today", "rule", "watch_id"; action is {flow, status: started|dropped|flow_not_active|flow_not_found|bad_with, run_id}); {"step":{"type":"notice","title":"No meal seen yet","text":{"$trigger":"message"},"priority"?:"urgent"}} or {"step":{"type":"speak","text":…}} runs one step from the workflow menu (needs interactions or speaker); or one of your own endpoint calls {method, path, body?, query?}, as a card's Bridgit.act would ({message} and {label} in its text are filled in). cooldown_s: default the rule's own time span

start_paused.description: Create the watch paused until resumed. Default false. A paused watch takes no readings and fires no rules.

min_readings.description: Readings to collect before the first question (default 3, at most window)

local.description: With camera in data: the free change check on the phone before any paid call. {change_check: true (default; false = pay for every photo), sensitivity: low | normal (default) | high (high notices smaller changes, so pays more often), learn_noise: true (default; when a paid call for a change gave the same answer, ignore those spots for 10 min), max_reuse_s: 30-3600 (default 300; ask again after this long even if nothing changed)}. A reused answer can still call you back (answered_locally: true). It looks at the photo only: other data you read doesn't make it pay

callback_url.description: Where to POST the result, as well as your registered callback and /v1/events. Same rules as callbacks: a tailnet address, or https on the internet if the owner allows internet callbacks. Signed with the callback_secret in the reply

repeat.description: false (default): one callback, then the watch ends. true: keep watching, at most one callback per cooldown_s

context.description: Anything Jev should know, up to 2000 characters ("the owner commutes by bike")

model.description: Who answers, and whether you pay: clef (Cloudflare Clef-omni, paid; the default with camera, about $0.000105 a photo), jev (TypeSafe, paid; the default without camera, about $0.000065 a photo, $0.000008 for text), glm (GLM 5.3 Flash through OpenRouter, paid), or none (local only, free: needs camera, takes no question, and calls you back when the picture changes). Paid models share the phone's hourly limit

camera.description: With camera in data: rear (default), front or an enrolled lan:<id> (needs lan_camera access)

situation.description: Instead of question: a common picture situation to spot and count on the camera, by library id (GET /v1/situations: dog_licking_itself, pot_boiling_over, sunlight_in_room, ...) or in your own words ("the cat is on the kitchen counter"), or {id | describe, alert?: true sends the owner an urgent notice when an episode starts (default: the library's choice; on for pot_boiling_over, smoke_in_room, water_on_floor), min?: 0-1 how likely to count, count_only_while?: a question like "Is a dog visible?"}. The phone fills in data ["camera"], the tuned question (id = the situation id, or "situation" for own words), a tally of episodes, the interval and the label; send model, camera, interval_s, max_paid_per_hour, expires_in_s, callback_when (on the situation id) or rules to change them, not question, questions or tally. Read the counts with GET /v1/watches/{id}/tally

interval_s.description: Seconds between readings: 30-3600 (default 60); down to 10 only for a camera tally with local.change_check enabled. Set max_paid_per_hour to bound optional model calls. A watch keeps the phone awake and reads location each time, so pick the longest interval and expiry that work. Phone-wide limit on paid watch checks, and the account's Jev and Clef calls an hour and monthly budget: read them with GET /v1/limits (they differ per account). A still, unplugged phone may pause checks until it wakes

question.description: A yes/no question in words, e.g. "Is the phone on a bicycle?". You're called back when Jev's probability of yes reaches min_probability. Send this or questions

label.description: A short name for logs and lists (default: the question)

max_paid_per_hour.description: At most this many paid model calls an hour for this watch, 1-240 (default: only the phone-wide limit). Checks over it are skipped, not paid. Also lowers what the watch takes from the phone-wide limit

people.description: With model none and camera in data: when the picture changes, take a short burst of photos, find faces on the phone, crop them (and embed them with an on-phone face model once it has downloaded) and hand them to the applet's private web portal. {burst: 1-5 (default 3; the changed photo counts), burst_gap_ms: 300-3000 (default 800), battery_floor: 0-100 (default 50; only while charging or at least this full), max_bursts_per_hour: 1-60 (default 20), min_face_share: 0.005-0.5 (default 0.01; smaller faces are ignored)}. Crops stay in memory only (at most 48, 6 hours). Needs repeat: true. Only in an installed applet's own plan with the people_seen permission the owner approved (refused here and from card actions), and it captures only while that applet's web portal is on with photo sharing

additional_cameras.description: Up to seven other enrolled camera ids or phone lenses. The watch rotates one per reading under its shared hourly cap; each source keeps its own change history. Excludes people watches.

min_probability.description: With question: how likely yes must be, 0-1 (default 0.8)

window.description: How many recent readings Jev sees, 1-20 (default 5)

callback_when.description: With questions: the answer that calls you back, 1-5 conditions that must all hold: {answer, min?, max?} on a noul probability, or {answer, choice, min_confidence?} (default 0.8) on a choice. Jev's confidence is not the probability: 0.67 likely is about 0.34 confident

tally.description: Count on the phone, for weeks, with you offline ("how many times did the dog eat today"). {track: the question id to count (default: your only question; with question, "match"), labels?: the choice options to count (default all), min_confidence?: 0-1 for a choice (default 0.5), min?: 0-1 for a noul, which counts as its own id when that likely (default 0.5), seen?: one condition, e.g. {answer: "dog_present", min: 0.6}; readings count, and add to watched time, only while it holds, gap_s?: readings this far apart are one episode (default 3 x interval_s, at least 60), label_gap_s?: map tracked labels to individual episode gaps in seconds (1-21600); coverage still uses gap_s, min_episode_readings?: drop shorter episodes (default 1), keep_days?: 1-30 (default 30)}. callback_when becomes optional (with it, callbacks come at most once per cooldown_s, and the watch never ends on a match). Read it with GET /v1/watches/{id}/tally; a card reads it with Bridgit.act, on a button or a timer of 5 minutes or more (each call is an action.executed event, and events keep only your newest 1,000)

200.description: 201: watch_id, label, created_at, expires_at, spec, callback_secret (only with callback_url; shown once), first_check_in_s (null while paused), delivery, usage. Each match is a watch.matched event {watch_id, label, question, answers, callback_when, model, answered_locally, cost_usd, checked_at, match, state (the readings the model saw), usage} (model none: change {largest_patch_share, sensitivity} instead of answers); the end is watch.ended {watch_id, reason: matched|expired|deleted|stopped_by_owner|access_revoked|budget|rejected|failing, message, checks, matches, usage, tally? (its last summary)}. A tally watch's rule firing is watch.rule {watch_id, label, rule, message, when, fired_at, today, action {method, path, ok, status, body} or null}. usage: {model, answered_locally (free checks), paid_calls, paid_cost_usd, paid_calls_last_hour, max_paid_per_hour, skipped_over_paid_cap, change_check}
